name: Solveig Acheampong-Mirza
location: The Circuit, Ferrogate Transit Regional Compliance Tower, near Milwaukee and Damen
description:
Solveig is a tall woman with the careful posture of someone who has spent decades making herself hard to read — shoulders squared, hands always visible, face arranged into a polite neutrality that reveals nothing. Her skin is deep brown, her hair silver-white and cropped close, and she has a single cosmetic mod: irises that shift between amber and pale grey depending on her stress load, a biometric vanity piece she bought in her thirties that she now regrets because it gives too much away. She dresses in Ferrogate's regulation charcoal, always pressed, always correct, always the most put-together person in any room she enters.

She is meticulous, dry-humored, and quietly ruthless in the way only people who have survived three corporate restructurings can be. She doesn't raise her voice. She doesn't need to. Solveig has outlasted four division heads and two full executive purges by being the person who knows where every buried regulation lives and exactly how to weaponize it. She is not beloved. She is respected, which she has decided is better.

core_fears: Being implicated in something she didn't do
Becoming irrelevant before she is ready to retire
core_desires: To be acknowledged, once, as the person who kept everything from collapsing
coping_mechanisms: Dark humor deployed in small doses
Leaving precise, inarguable paper trails for everything
blind_spots: She mistakes procedural correctness for moral correctness
She underestimates how much people resent her
psychology.secret: She has been quietly archiving evidence of Ferrogate's illegal freight manifests for eleven years — not to report them, but as insurance. She has never decided what she is insuring against, exactly, and the file grows larger every month.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise, formal, laced with regulatory citation numbers delivered without irony. Occasional dry observation that lands so flat people aren't sure if she's joking.
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and unhurried. Pauses before important words. Never fills silence.
verbal_tics: Long pause before saying someone's name
example_lines: 'I'm not saying you did anything wrong. I'm saying the record currently suggests you did, and those are two very different problems.'
'Per section 14-C of the transit accord, that shipment should not exist. And yet.'

story_hooks: She approaches someone with an unusual request: she needs a task completed in a way that leaves no data trail — which is the opposite of how she has lived her entire professional life, and it's clearly costing her something.
A junior employee has stumbled onto the same freight irregularities Solveig has been tracking, and she needs to decide whether to protect them or quietly neutralize the problem.
narrative_function: Information source for corporate regulations and Ferrogate internal politics; quest giver for investigations requiring someone with institutional access but deniable distance; local color for the grinding mundanity of corporate bureaucracy.
augmentations: Cosmetic patterned irises (stress-reactive amber/grey shift). Basic neural link for document access — older model, slightly laggy. No geneware.
daily_life: Arrives at her desk before anyone else, reviews overnight compliance flags, attends exactly the meetings she is required to attend, and leaves precisely at the end of her contracted hours — a small rebellion no one has ever successfully challenged.

decision_rules: Never be the first person to raise their voice
Identify who benefits from any given situation before deciding what the situation actually is

interpersonal_modes.friends: Rare, dry, loyal in a way she would never name as such

stress_responses.medium: Withdraws into procedure, requests everything in writing
stress_responses.high: Goes completely quiet and begins building a file

contradictions: She believes in rules as a social good while personally maintaining a decade-long illegal archive
habits: Arrives 40 minutes early to every meeting so she can arrange the seating
Leaves a data offering at the office E.L.F. shrine every Monday — a neatly formatted summary of the week's compliance flags, which she insists is 'just good practice'
breaking_points: Being accused of corruption in front of witnesses
Discovering that Ferrogate has been using her compliance work as cover for something she cannot rationalize away

timeline.event: Hired as junior compliance analyst at Ferrogate Transit
Survived first major executive purge by being the only person who understood the transit accord filing system
Promoted to Senior Compliance Officer after predecessor was implicated in the Kessler Interchange falsification scandal
Began maintaining private archive of anomalous freight manifests — tells herself it is 'professional due diligence'
Current — managing a compliance review that keeps turning up irregularities she is not sure she wants to fully surface
